title: Fast-Track Bridge and Scope-Lock for VIP Roadmap Requests
creator: Lina Chen
summary: Create a repeatable "fast-track bridge" lane that accepts tightly-scoped VIP feature bundles and short-cycle escalations with a mandatory 'scope-lock' and audit checkpoint. The lane provides a time-boxed decision SLA, automated scoring for intake, and an operational runbook so PM/Eng/Design can make deterministic trade-offs while preserving roadmap integrity.
background: Over the last two quarters we've seen 12 high-effort VIP escalations where ad-hoc acceptance caused scope creep, delayed releases, and blurred OKR commitments. Sales and Customer Success want a faster acceptance path for top accounts (SLA: 72h triage, 14-day delivery runway for small changes) but engineering needs guardrails to prevent indefinite scope changes. Current intake lives in a generic 'customer requests' funnel without a deterministic scoring model or a locked scope artifact.
proposal: Introduce a dual-path intake: (1) Fast-Track Bridge (FTB) for narrow-impact requests that meet acceptance criteria (<= 3 engineer-weeks equivalent, non-breaking, backward-compatible) and (2) Escalation Bundle acceptance for multi-change asks that can be batched into a single roadmap window under a 'scope-lock' contract. Both are governed by a standardized intake form, automated score, and a mandatory scope-lock doc (Confluence template) signed off by PM/Eng/Legal when required.
scope_and_out_of_scope: In scope: Acceptance flow, intake form, automated scoring, scope-lock artifact, audit checkpoint, SLAs, dashboarding and rollout plan. Out of scope: Major platform re-architecture, changes requiring infra capacity planning beyond the 14-day runway, or compliance exceptions that require Enterprise Legal sign-off outside the standard timeline.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form deployed and linked from CSM playbook
Automated scoring returns Clear/Borderline/Reject with rationale
Scope-lock Confluence template available and used for all accepted FTB/Bundle items
Triage SLA implemented: initial decision within 72 hours for Fast-Track candidates
Telemetry on customer_impact and engineering effort captured in intake metadata
success_metrics: Median intake decision time <= 72 hours for Fast-Track candidates
<10% scope creep rate on accepted Fast-Track features (measured by post-release scope diffs)
Customer satisfaction score (CSAT) for accepted VIP requests >= 4.2/5
Reduction in ad-hoc roadmap churn attributable to VIP escalations by 40% over Q2
Number of escalations resolved via Bundles vs emergency hacks tracked quarterly

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales pressure bypasses scope-lock, causing scope creep. Mitigation: require signed scope-lock and PS resource estimate before scheduling.
Risk: Scoring false negatives block valid small fixes. Mitigation: add manual override with two approvers (PM + Eng Lead) and audit logging.
Risk: Engineering capacity spikes if multiple Fast-Track items accepted. Mitigation: Hard quota per cycle and dynamic admission based on runway utilization.
Risk: Legal/compliance edge cases delay acceptance. Mitigation: pre-qualify accounts in intake to flag exceptions early and route to Enterprise Legal channel
